description: Add notes textarea to POS template (templates/orders/pos.html) and wire it into the JavaScript POS object (static/js/main.js). The backend view create_pos_order in apps/orders/views.py already reads notes=data.get('notes', '') — only the frontend needs changes.
steps:
1. Edit templates/orders/pos.html — Add a notes textarea inside the .pos-checkout-controls div. Insert it AFTER the closing of the payment method row (after line ~269) and BEFORE the closing of .pos-checkout-controls (line ~270). Use this exact markup:
Also add a mobile CSS rule for the notes textarea near the existing #pos-customer-name rule (around line 133): #pos-notes { min-height: 44px; font-size: 0.9rem; } The .pos-layout--collapsed hidden controls block (around line 156-163) already hides .pos-checkout-controls wholesale, so the notes textarea is included automatically — no extra CSS rule needed.
acceptance_criteria: The POS checkout panel shows a labeled multiline textarea with id='pos-notes' below the payment method row.
The placeholder reads 'Add special instructions or notes for this order...'
The notes field has maxlength='1000' to enforce a practical client-side limit.
Placing a POS order with notes text results in the notes being saved to Order.notes in the database.
Placing a POS order without notes (textarea empty) succeeds without error; Order.notes is ''.
After a successful POS order, the notes field is cleared along with the customer name field.
Refreshing the POS page before submitting restores the notes text from the draft (sessionStorage).
python manage.py test apps.orders --verbosity=2 passes all existing tests.
